description.narrative: Stakeholder Effect: Increased access to finance for MSMEs, including Agri-MSMEs and WMSMEs: IFC anticipates that this Project will enable CBC to expand financing to MSMEs, including Agri-MSMEs and WMSMEs, which are underserved in Sri Lanka, mainly due to lack of collateral and information gaps. These underserved clients include WMSMEs or agricultural households in rural and semiurban areas, with financing needs for supporting income generation or livelihood, as well as borrowers requiring funding for climate risk mitigation projects. The proposed long-term facility above will enable CBC to expand longer term lending to these underserved segments. Improved MSME access to finance is expected to stimulate firm growth and contribute to Sri Lanka's post-crisis economic recovery. Contribution to Market Creation - Competitiveness: Commercial banks in Sri Lanka have historically been reluctant to lend long-term to MSMEs, which are perceived as high-risk. IFC anticipates that the project will promote greater competitiveness in the financial sector by encouraging other FIs to scale up their longer term MSME lending, including to WMSMEs and borrowers operating in the agricultural sector.

The proposed investment consists of a five-year, USD-denominated, amortizing, senior unsecured syndicated loan of up to US$200 million, comprising: (i) an IFC A-loan of up to US$100 million (gross amount) and (ii) mobilization of up to US$100 million through a parallel loan structure, a B-loan structure, or a combination of B and parallel structures, to Commercial Bank of Ceylon PLC (CBC), the largest private commercial bank in Sri Lanka and an IFC and AMC equity investee. The proceeds of the loan will be used for on lending to micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), including agriculture MSMEs, smallholder farmers, and farmer cooperatives (in line with the AgriConnect requirements), and women owned MSMEs (WMSMEs). IFC's support to CBC confirms IFC's countercyclical role in Sri Lanka's recovery process. In particular, the Project is expected to signal confidence in the country's recovering financial sector, which has been hit by multiple shocks over the past five years. As the country's recovery strengthens, the proposed IFC investment is anticipated to enhance CBC's ability to support economic growth and job creation.

name.narrative: CBC is headquartered in Colombo, Sri Lanka and has 272 branches spread across the Sri Lanka and another 20 branches in Bangladesh. The bank also operates 974 ATMs and CRMs and has a total staff strength of over 5,700. The project proceeds would be utilized for borrowers in Sri Lanka.
